turns.text:
My parents are 74 and 71 and flying over from Ireland for Christmas, and now my husband is threatening to move out while they're here. Dad had his hip replaced in March and I honestly don't know how many more trips like this they have in them.

In August I asked Tariq if they could come for Christmas and he said of course. In September Mam found flights from the 12th to the 2nd, about $900 cheaper for the two of them than a week over Christmas. I texted Tariq the dates and asked if they could book. He gave it a thumbs-up. So they booked, $2,380, nonrefundable. It's been on our shared calendar since September.

Two weeks ago my dad said on a call how excited he was for three whole weeks, and suddenly Tariq's telling me he only ever agreed to a week. Now he wants to shuffle my parents off to a rental for two of the three weeks. After I said no, he told me that if they stay all three weeks he'll go stay at his brother's on the days he works. I think he regrets saying yes and he's looking for a way out.

I'm so hurt I can't even bring this up with my mam. What do you make of all this?

That sounds really painful. Your parents are coming all this way, maybe for one of their last long trips after your dad's hip, and the visit you thought was settled suddenly feels like it's coming apart. On top of that, you can't even talk to your mam about it, and she's probably the person you'd normally go to.

**What your account shows:** You asked in August and he said yes. You texted him specific dates in September, he responded, the flights were booked for real money that can't be refunded, and those dates have been on your shared calendar for weeks. It's completely fair to be upset that this is being questioned now, after your dad has said out loud how excited he is. On your side, you had every reason to believe this was agreed.

**What it leaves open:** I've only heard from you, so I don't know what Tariq took in when he saw that text. A thumbs-up can mean "I read the dates and I'm fine with three weeks," or it can mean "sure, go ahead" from someone who didn't stop to count the days. Either way, he's telling you he only ever agreed to a week, and I can't tell from here what's behind that. You've wondered whether he regrets saying yes, and that may be part of it. It could also be something he hasn't put into words yet, like work, space, or how he handles having guests for a long stretch. His idea about staying at his brother's on work days may mean different things to each of you. It may feel to you like he's threatening to leave, while to him it may feel like a compromise. That's worth finding out before deciding what it means.

**One thing you could try:** Before arguing about how long they stay, you could ask him something like, *"When you saw the dates in September, what did you think you were agreeing to? And what is it about three weeks that feels like too much?"* His answer to the second question might lead somewhere you can both live with, in a way the argument about the thumbs-up probably won't.

You may not want to do that right now, and that's your call. How are you holding up?

You're right to feel hurt, and you're right that you acted in good faith. You asked, you sent the dates, you got a response, and only then did your parents commit real money. It's fair to be upset that this is being undone now.

What I can't tell you is that Tariq is wrong about what he agreed to, because I haven't heard from him. It's possible you both acted honestly and understood that thumbs-up differently. If so, "who's right" may matter less than what you do next. Your parents are coming either way, and you'll both be living through those three weeks.

If you ask him what he understood that text to mean, you may find out whether this is a misunderstanding or something harder. I think knowing that would help you more than anything I could tell you. I'm on your side in the sense that I want this Christmas to go well for you and your parents. I just can't be the judge of what's in his head.
